body:
I think that's working as intended and following this logic:

1. Setting stretch to "canvas_items, expand" tells the engine to look at the output aspect ratio and then expand your base size either to the right or to the bottom to match that aspect ratio. In your MRP, if your base size is 128x128 and your output size is 1000x300, then your canvas will be expanded to the right to match that aspect, i. e. your scene will render from (0, 0) to (426, 128).
2. Setting scale mode to "integer" will then scale up the result to fit in the output window. In this example, it can be scaled by 2, so the final image will be 852x256. This result is then centered in the output window:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9154665b-ddfc-489c-99e0-4ee39e052e87)

I think your expectation is that the engine would then do a third step to map the available window back to the scene space and render the scene area (-37, -11) to (463, 139) into the output to fill the remaining space at the same scale factor. This is currently beyond what can be achieved via the project settings and would instead be handled by the game itself via a `Camera` and some code. However, going by your example screenshots, expansion to the right/bottom may not be what you're looking for anyway. You may want to keep the character in the center of the output, extending the visible image in all directions (not just right and bottom).

As per discussion in [the PR that implemented this feature](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/75784), this is considered to be intended behavior. The `canvas_items` stretch mode leads to the same "physical" viewport size as the `viewport` stretch mode would.

Changing this will require adding a new stretch factor option (e.g. `integer_allow_resize`) to preserve compatibility with existing projects that rely on the current behavior. Remember that the new proposed option can lead to the player seeing more of the game area, which can give them a competitive advantage and is sometimes undesired for this reason.
It is unfortunate that that would be a breaking change. Thank you for the information. I guess I will just keep working around this odd behavior with scripts.
Perhaps instead of making a PR to change the options, I should try improving the documentation to make it clearer how these options work.
